chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: No overseas travel; Armstrong drops the big band
summary: McRae never went overseas in the war; Armstrong later cut the big band for an all-star group after complaining of arrangement costs.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, in all the band experience that you had, Teddy, did you travel overseas anytime before -- say before the war ended itself? Before you went out with your own band and started (inaudible) --
You didn't have any overseas travel.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Louie came back in about a year after I left the band.
I was still working -- still doing some things with Joe Glaser, you know. And he was just -- we were talking about Louie and the ideas of things.

One day I walked in, he was screaming about all the money he had spent on the arrangements. I say, "Well, those are your ideas," you know, "because you were doing these for the song pluggers and getting things over the air (inaudible)."
But -- I say, "Well if you discussed it with the band, why don't you build Louie an all-star band?"
He say, "Yeah, that's an idea." And I just let it go at that.
Next time I knew it, he had -- Louie had Kyle got rid of the big band. Had Billy (inaudible) and all those guys with him, you know.
